Quite for Facebook

A feed of the people you actually know.

Sponsored posts, suggested pages and groups you never joined are taken out of your feed. What is left is the people you actually follow.

Free MIT ChromeEdgeBraveArc

Add to Chrome, it's free View the source ›

1 permission · Runs only on Facebook · No tracking · MIT licensed

Quite for Facebook strips out the things you never asked to see: posts marked Sponsored or Ad, pages you do not follow pushed into your feed, groups you are not a member of, and the ad panel sitting above your contacts on the right.

What it leaves alone matters just as much. Your own posts, your friends' posts, groups you are in and pages you already follow are never touched. Nothing is blocked, unfollowed or reported on your behalf. Posts are hidden from view, and everything comes straight back the moment you switch it off.

What it does

6 things, and no more.

Ads out of the feed

Anything marked Sponsored or Ad is hidden as the page builds, so it never reaches you in the first place.

Suggested posts gone

Pages you do not follow, pushed into your feed by the algorithm, stop appearing. Strict mode narrows this to posts explicitly marked "Suggested for you".

The Sponsored column

The advertising panel on the right, above your contacts, goes with the rest of it.

Your people stay put

Your posts, your friends' posts, groups you are in and pages you follow are never touched. Nothing is unfollowed or reported on your behalf.

See what was caught

Turn on the placeholder option and each hidden post leaves a small strip with a Show button, so you can check nothing you wanted has been swept up.

A running count

The popup keeps a tally of the ads, suggested posts and groups it has hidden for you, with Copy report, Show all and Reset underneath.

Installing it

One click from the Chrome Web Store. The unpacked route below still works if you would rather run the source.

Add to Chrome

  1. 1

    On GitHub, click the green Code button, choose Download ZIP, and unzip it. You need the folder. Keep it somewhere permanent, because moving or deleting it stops the extension working.

  2. 2

    Open chrome://extensions in your browser.

  3. 3

    Turn on Developer mode, top right.

  4. 4

    Click Load unpacked and select the folder you unzipped.

  5. 5

    Reload any Facebook tab you already had open.

Chrome shows a "Developer mode extensions" warning each time it starts. That is normal for anything installed outside the Web Store, and it can be dismissed.

30 August 2026 New Quite for Facebook

Quite for Facebook is on the Chrome Web Store

Quite for Facebook hides the clutter from your feed and does nothing else: posts marked Sponsored or Ad, suggested posts from pages you do not follow, suggested groups, and the Sponsored column on the right.

Two options are worth knowing about. Strict mode only hides posts that are also marked “Suggested for you”, for anyone who wants it to err on the cautious side. A placeholder option leaves a small strip with a Show button where a post was, so you can always see what was hidden and put it back, which is also the honest way to check it is not hiding things you wanted.

It runs only on facebook.com. It has no account and no server, and nothing is sent to us.

It is free, MIT licensed, and the source is on GitHub.

What it asks for

1 permission and one site, and why each is there.

storage
To remember your checkbox settings, and a running count of what it has hidden or skipped. Settings use Chrome's own extension-settings sync, so with Chrome sync on they travel with your Chrome profile.
*://*.facebook.com/*
The extension runs on Facebook and nowhere else. It has no permission to read, or even see, any other site you visit.

Chrome shows you this list at install time. We would rather you saw it first. The source is public, so you can check that it is the whole list.

Questions

It hid a post I wanted to see.

Facebook shows a Follow button on any page post you do not already follow, including one a friend shared, so those get caught too. Turn on Strict mode and it will only remove posts explicitly marked "Suggested for you". Fewer suggestions disappear, but nothing you actually follow will.

Ads have started appearing again.

Facebook disguises the labels this relies on and changes the disguise periodically. When that happens ads reappear until the extension is updated. Expected rather than a regression.

Does it unfollow or block anything?

No. Nothing is blocked, unfollowed or reported on your behalf. Posts are hidden from view and everything returns the moment you switch it off.

How do I tell which version is running?

Click the extension icon. The version shown is the one actually running in the page. If it does not match what you installed, Chrome is serving an old build. Hit reload on chrome://extensions, then reload Facebook.
